A_target.statement:
Let $T$ be a [[Definition:Consistent|consistent]] [[Definition:Theory (Logic)|theory]] of [[Definition:Propositional Logic|classical logic]].
Let $\mathrm {Form}$ be the set of [[Definition:Well-Formed Formula|formulas]] and $\phi \equiv_T \psi \iff T \vdash \phi \leftrightarrow \psi$.
Then $\mathrm {Form} / \equiv_T$ is a [[Definition:Boolean Algebra|Boolean algebra]], the [[Definition:Lindenbaum-Tarski Algebra|Lindenbaum-Tarski algebra]] of $T$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\theta$ be a [[Definition:Congruence Relation|congruence]] on an [[Definition:Algebraic Structure|algebraic structure]] $A$.
Then $A / \theta$ carries the operations of $A$, defined on representatives.

substitutions.the structure being collapsed: the set of formulas with conjunction, disjunction, and negation
substitutions.the quotient structure: the Lindenbaum-Tarski algebra of the theory

derived.the operations descend to the quotient: the connectives are well defined on equivalence classes
derived.the axioms are inherited: the Boolean algebra laws hold because their instances are provable

validity_conditions: Provable equivalence is an equivalence relation and is compatible with the connectives, since equivalent formulas may be substituted inside a conjunction, disjunction, or negation.
The Boolean algebra axioms hold in the quotient because each corresponding equivalence is provable in the theory.
Consistency is required for the algebra to be nondegenerate; in an inconsistent theory all formulas are provably equivalent and the algebra collapses to one element.
proof_plan: Regard $\mathrm {Form}$ as an algebra with operations $\land$, $\lor$, $\neg$ and constants $\top$, $\bot$.

If $T \vdash \phi \leftrightarrow \phi'$ and $T \vdash \psi \leftrightarrow \psi'$, then:
:$T \vdash \paren {\phi \land \psi} \leftrightarrow \paren {\phi' \land \psi'}$
and similarly for $\lor$ and $\neg$.
Hence $\equiv_T$ is a [[Definition:Congruence Relation|congruence]].
Collapse by $\equiv_T$, so the connectives descend to the classes $\eqclass \phi {}$.
